title: Nadia Beller, Victim and Ex-Partner of Fernando Cerimedo, Takes Asylum in the Mexican Embassy in Bolivia
author: La Jornada Staff
content:
_This article by[La Jornada
Staff](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/de%20la%20redacci%C3%B3n) originally
appeared in the [November 9, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/09/politica/nadia-beller-
victima-y-expareja-de-fernando-cerimedo-se-asila-en-la-embajada-de-mexico-en-
bolivia), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

Nadia Beller, the victim of an attempted femicide by her ex-partner, the
Argentine far-right adviser Fernando Cerimedo, founder of La Derecha Diario,
**has taken asylum in the Mexican Embassy in Bolivia**.

This was announced in a statement by the Bolivian Ministry of Foreign Affairs,
which noted that **the Mexican government notified it of the asylum on
November 4** , along with a request for a safe-conduct pass.

The Bolivian Foreign Ministry stated that, within the framework of the 30th
Ibero-American Summit, held in Madrid, Mexico's Secretary of Foreign Affairs,
Roberto Velasco, and Bolivia's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Héctor Francisco
Huanca Gutiérrez, held a bilateral meeting. However, it clarified that during
the meeting “**no commitment whatsoever was made to grant the requested safe-
conduct** , nor was it agreed to deliver it upon the Bolivian Foreign
Minister's return to the country.”

It also indicated that the request is under evaluation by the competent
authorities, in accordance with the provisions of the national legal system
and the applicable international obligations. So far, it stated, no decision
has been made nor has a formal response been issued on the matter.

## Why Did Nadia Beller Ask Mexico for Asylum?

According to _Brújula Streaming_ , Beller said that, due to constant
harassment, on October 29 she requested the withdrawal of the police guard
from her home in Santa Cruz, but did not renounce her status as a protected
witness. She added that the following day the prosecutor's office notified the
Police to comply with that request, although **the officers remained at the
location until November 5 or 6**.

> Since they didn't feel like obeying a prosecutor's order, I didn't feel like
> letting them run my life and harass me. And what I did was seek my own
> safety in one of the four countries that offered me asylum.
>
> Nadia Beller, in an interview with _Brújula Streaming_

The lawyer indicated that the other countries offered her alternatives that,
according to her account, involved leaving Bolivia through illegal crossings
or carrying out longer procedures. However, she did not specify which nations
they were.
